import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyCircleProductCup
import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyPoint
import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyZeroConnected

/-!
# The antipodal generator of the circle's first cohomology

Specializing the circle-product decomposition to a point identifies the first
integral singular cohomology of the circle with the integers. The class defined
by the connecting map of the first ordered overlap component maps to one.
This fixes the sign by the antipodal chart coordinates; comparison with a
positively oriented complex loop is a separate statement.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

attribute [local instance 2000] Prod.instModule

open CategoryTheory

namespace Mumford.Analytic

/-- The circle class obtained from the first ordered antipodal overlap
component, after identifying `Unit × Circle` with the circle. -/
def circleAntipodalClass (v : Circle) :
    IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of Circle) 1 :=
  singularCohomologyPullback
    (TopCat.ofHom ⟨fun z : Circle => ((), z), continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id⟩) 1
    (circleProductConnectingClass (TopCat.of Unit) v)

/-- The first integral singular cohomology of the circle is the integers,
normalized by the ordered antipodal overlap. -/
def circleCohomologyEquivInt (v : Circle) :
    IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of Circle) 1 ≃ₗ[ℤ] ℤ := by
  letI := integralSingularCohomology_subsingleton (X := TopCat.of Unit) 0
  letI : Unique (IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of Unit) 1) :=
    ⟨⟨0⟩, fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
  exact (singularCohomologyHomotopyEquiv
    (X := TopCat.of (Unit × Circle)) (Y := TopCat.of Circle)
    (Homeomorph.uniqueProd Unit Circle).toHomotopyEquiv 1).trans
    ((circleProductCohomologyEquiv (TopCat.of Unit) v 0).trans
      (LinearEquiv.uniqueProd.trans (singularZeroCohomologyEquivInt (TopCat.of Unit) ())))

/-- The antipodal connecting class maps to one in the integer coordinate. -/
@[simp] theorem circleCohomologyEquivInt_antipodalClass (v : Circle) :
    circleCohomologyEquivInt v (circleAntipodalClass v) = 1 := by
  have h : singularCohomologyHomotopyEquiv
      (X := TopCat.of (Unit × Circle)) (Y := TopCat.of Circle)
      (Homeomorph.uniqueProd Unit Circle).toHomotopyEquiv 1
      (circleAntipodalClass v) = circleProductConnectingClass (TopCat.of Unit) v :=
    (singularCohomologyHomotopyEquiv
      (X := TopCat.of (Unit × Circle)) (Y := TopCat.of Circle)
      (Homeomorph.uniqueProd Unit Circle).toHomotopyEquiv 1).apply_symm_apply _
  change singularZeroCohomologyEquivInt (TopCat.of Unit) ()
    ((circleProductCohomologyEquiv (TopCat.of Unit) v 0
      (singularCohomologyHomotopyEquiv
        (X := TopCat.of (Unit × Circle)) (Y := TopCat.of Circle)
        (Homeomorph.uniqueProd Unit Circle).toHomotopyEquiv 1
        (circleAntipodalClass v))).2) = 1
  rw [h, circleProductConnectingClass, circleProductCohomologyEquiv_apply_connecting,
    sub_zero]
  simp

end Mumford.Analytic
